title: Chat Completions v1 -> Redwood API translation layer (request/response normalizer)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a translation/normalization layer that accepts incoming OpenAI Chat Completions v1-style requests and maps them to Redwood's internal API model, and vice versa for responses. This layer must preserve streaming semantics, function/tool-calling behavior, structured output conventions, and telemetry for cost/latency while avoiding changes to existing Redwood SDK surface or breaking hosted customers.

Scope:
- Request mapping: roles, name/id semantics, message arrays, system/user/assistant handling, temperature/top_p mappings, max_tokens -> max_new_tokens translation, stop tokens handling, and function call hints.
- Streaming: accept OpenAI delta-stream chunks, aggregate/normalize into Redwood streaming frames; preserve chunk ordering and function-call delta emission.
- Function/tool calling: translate OpenAI function schema into Redwood tool descriptors, support both explicit and "auto" function_call behaviors, and ensure we emit structured function_call events for downstream routers.
- Responses: map Redwood outputs (content, tools, structured JSON outputs) back into the Chat Completions response shape while keeping consumption patterns identical for OpenAI-compatible clients.
- Metrics & billing: expose per-token accounting consistent with Redwood usage reporting; add flags to attribute requests to compatibility layer.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: SDK-level client helpers, non-chat endpoints, and migration of customers to native Redwood API surface. Those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 requests are accepted by the compatibility endpoint and return the same success codes as OpenAI for happy-path requests.

Streaming responses from Redwood runtime are transformed into delta events that match OpenAI streaming envelopes (role/content/function_call deltas) and are emitted in order with identical termination tokens/close events.

Function calling: when a model requests a function, the compatibility layer emits an OpenAI-style function_call object; inbound function_call responses from clients are correctly attached to the running completion and forwarded to runtime execution.
Stop-token semantics: both single and multiple stop tokens provided in v1 requests are honored; Redwood stop configuration maps correctly and does not truncate tokens unexpectedly.
Telemetry: request and response usage fields (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) are available in the proxied response metadata and match test harness outputs within 1% tolerance.
No regressions for native Redwood API users; compatibility layer is behind a separate route and feature-flagged for internal testing before GA.
Integration tests covering streaming, sync, function call, and error edge cases pass in CI.
technical_notes: Request mapping details: map messages[] -> Redwood.messages but preserve message.name when present; convert OpenAI 'role: system' into Redwood 'system' metadata and ensure initial system prompt precedence is first in the serialized request.

Temperature/top_p/max_tokens mappings: convert max_tokens in OpenAI request to Redwood.max_new_tokens; if both max_tokens and max_new_tokens present, prefer explicit Redwood field. Provide translation table in //docs/compatibility/params.md.

Streaming protocol: OpenAI emits 'data: {...}\n\n' SSE chunks. Implement a chunk emitter that consumes Redwood runtime stream frames and re-encodes into OpenAI SSE envelopes. Pay attention to partial UTF-8 codepoints when slicing token deltas. Include sequence numbers in debug logs only (not emitted to client).

Function call translation: OpenAI function schema (name, description, parameters) -> Redwood tool descriptor. Persist a tool_catalog_id mapping for local tools. When the model emits function_call deltas, emit the same sequence of delta events: first name field then arguments field as they arrive. When client supplies a function result, translate it into Redwood tool invocation and attach call metadata (call_id, origin=compat(v1)).

Structured outputs: Redwood structured responses (json_schema/format) should be mirrored in the 'message.content' field and additional 'message.function_call' as per OpenAI shape. Avoid embedding Redwood-only fields into top-level OpenAI response; use response.metadata.compat to include debugging info if requested via ?debug=true.

Error mapping: Redwood error codes map to OpenAI-like HTTP 4xx/5xx where possible, e.g., quota -> 429, invalid_arg -> 400, not_found -> 404, internal -> 500. Include 'error.type' and 'error.param' keys in response following OpenAI conventions.

Concurrency & ordering: Redwood runtime may send batched tokens for efficiency. The translator must preserve original token ordering per-request and must not interleave tokens across concurrent requests. Implement per-request buffer and ordered emission with backpressure.
Performance: target <5ms median overhead for non-streaming requests and <8ms added latency per streaming chunk emission under p95. Add microbenchmarks in /bench/compat-layer.
Telemetry and billing: add 'compat_layer=true' tag to request logs and usage metrics. Ensure token counting uses the same tokenizer version as Redwood runtime to avoid mismatch.
migration_plan: Create feature-flagged compatibility route /v1/chat/completions that routes through the translation layer (internal-only).
Run shadow traffic for 48 hours with sampling to validate mapping (log differences).
Enable end-to-end integration tests and QA validation with a small set of internal customers.
Roll to beta customers with opt-in; collect telemetry and fix discrepancies in token accounting and function-call ordering.
Gradually increase traffic, keep rollback plan ready to flip flag and route traffic back to native Redwood API.
test_plan: Unit tests for request/response field mappings (100% coverage for mappings).
Streaming harness: inject synthetic runtime token streams with partial function_call deltas; assert OpenAI SSE envelopes emitted identical to spec.
Function-call roundtrip: simulate model requesting function, client returning function result; assert tool invocation recorded and final response shape matches OpenAI expectation.
Fuzz stop-token handling: randomized stop list and prompt shapes to verify no early termination regressions.
Integration: full e2e against runtime-2.3 in staging with token accounting comparison tooling.
